How to read this realtime check

Source: KITTI tracking development sequence 0012, 78 consecutive frames at 10 FPS (7.8 seconds). Each frame is decoded and processed again on every run. Bounding boxes, depth, range and TTC come from the fixed saved models; they are not attached from KITTI labels.

Real time here means keeping pace with this 10 FPS source. It does not establish 30 FPS camera operation. Turn off source pacing to inspect maximum observed browser playback rate. Startup, server processing and browser transport affect wall time. Pauses are excluded from the active display-rate counter. Manual steps do not count as continuous playback.

This is prerecorded video: a braking command cannot change its future frames. The separate 3D simulation is the control-loop task. The distance model requires matching camera calibration. The saved tracker assumes 10 Hz, so this mode rejects other frame rates/resolutions. TTC is optical-axis closing time, not a collision guarantee. KITTI imagery: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
